[the rule's own record before the fold]
kb/Work PB489 LANDED - BOTH HALVES OF GR7 b)'s RESTRICTION NOW HOLD. (i) 'may be referenced only in PROCEDURE DIVISION statements' is enforced: a LINAGE-COUNTER written in a file description entry's LINAGE clause is refused at bind with COBOL2024 naming 8.4.3.14.3 SR1, where it used to compile clean and die at OPEN with the nonsense message "LINAGE operand 'LPF' is not resolvable to storage" - the binder had taken the FILE-NAME QUALIFIER for the data-name. (ii) 'only the input-output control system may change the value' now rejects by its OWN rule: ExpressionBinder.ResolveReceiving grew the missing third arm, COBOL2026 citing 8.4.3.14.3 SR2 and 13.18.34.4 GR7 b). It was the two-arm-dispatch shape with the third arm absent - LINE-COUNTER had a rule-citing rejection and PAGE-COUNTER a correctly-labelled not-yet-implemented, while LINAGE-COUNTER, the only one of the three that is flatly ILLEGAL as a receiver, inherited the generic COBOL0899 catch-all and told the user that permanently illegal source was a feature awaiting implementation; the named test asserts COBOL0899 is no longer among the diagnostics. Everything the adjudication recorded as already implemented and covered is unchanged: GR7 a)'s per-file counter, the counter's meaning under GR7 c), and both arms of GR7 b)'s qualification requirement including the PB123 GLOBAL-FD sweep.

[folded GR-13.18.34.4-L2.1 = §13.18.34.4 7) c) 1.: CONFORMS]
kb/Work PB578 LANDED - THE IMPLICIT-INCREMENT SENTENCE IS NOW MODELLED, AND IT WAS OBSERVABLE. Sentence 1 ('automatically reset to one') is unchanged and pinned by LinageConformanceTests.Gr7c1_AdvancingPageResetsCounterToOne. Sentence 2 ('During the resetting of LINAGE-COUNTER to the value one, the value of LINAGE-COUNTER is implicitly incremented to exceed the value specified by integer-1 or the data item referenced by data-name-1', cite.py --check 13.18.34.4 -> OK 7) c) 1.) puts the counter past the page size, which is 14.9.51.4 GR26 a)'s trigger ('This occurs when the associated LINAGE-COUNTER is equal to or exceeds the page size', OK 26)), so ADVANCING PAGE is a PAGE OVERFLOW: GR27 a) sets EC-I-O-EOP-OVERFLOW to exist and GR28 keeps a NOT END-OF-PAGE imperative from running. The old derivation's step (c) was wrong twice over: GR27 a)'s EC-I-O-EOP-OVERFLOW is observable WITHOUT the END-OF-PAGE phrase (a USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION declarative, an exception-checking PERFORM's WHEN, FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS), and SR18 bars only the AT phrase, so a NOT END-OF-PAGE phrase beside ADVANCING PAGE is legal source - which the compiler REJECTED (COBOL0861) and which, had it compiled, would have run its imperative. SequentialConnector.PositionOnLogicalPage now sends ADVANCING PAGE through the ONE overflow arm (lines < 0 || counter + lines > page body): one transition, one reset, one EC-I-O-EOP-OVERFLOW. THE NOTE'S HOLE, re-probed: the declarative now fires (pb526_linage_ec_condition) and, on a GR6 b) 2 violation during ADVANCING PAGE, reads GR6 b) 2's 0, never the transient value (the WRITE is unsuccessful, so no end-of-page condition either). Determination: docs/CONFORMANCE.md §4 'WRITE ADVANCING PAGE on a logical page is a page overflow'. Witnesses: conformance:cases/8.4.3.14-LINAGE-COUNTER/pb578_advancing_page_overflow_85 (NOT EOP silent on AFTER and BEFORE ADVANCING PAGE, live on a plain write), conformance:cases/8.4.3.14-LINAGE-COUNTER/pb578_advancing_page_eop_overflow (the EC-I-O-EOP-OVERFLOW declarative reads LINAGE-COUNTER 001; the violation declarative reads 000). || code site: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/IO/SequentialConnector.cs#PositionOnLogicalPage

[folded GR-13.18.34.4-L2.2 = §13.18.34.4 7) c) 2.: CONFORMS]
BOTH OPERAND FORMS MEASURED. The integer form is the named test (1 + 3 = 4) and the zero case is conformance-test:WiseOwl.Cobol.Tests.Conformance.LinageConformanceTests.Gr25c_AdvancingZero_CounterUnchanged. The IDENTIFIER form - the half the rule states separately and no repo test exercises - was probed: <lane3 scratch>/out-b3/probe/linage/p24_ident.cob does `WRITE ... AFTER ADVANCING WS-N LINES` with WS-N = 3 then `BEFORE ADVANCING WS-N LINES` with WS-N = 2 on a 9-line body and reads back LINAGE-COUNTER 4 then 6, i.e. the item's CURRENT contents at each write, and BEFORE and AFTER both count. || CORRECTED 2026-09-06 by kb/Work PB712. This note used to say the 2023 combined BEFORE+AFTER form increments the counter by n+m through two separate AdvanceLinageCounter calls. It does not, and the spelling it described is not one 14.9.51.2 Format 1 prints: the printed phrase's choice indicators enclose only the WORDS BEFORE and AFTER, ADVANCING and its operand sit outside them ONCE, and 14.9.51.4 GR25 a) advances the page 'the number of lines equal to that value' -- ONE advance, which GR25 e)/f) merely PLACE. The combined form now increments by n, exactly as a lone BEFORE does, through the ONE WriteAdvancing call; tests/conformance/2023/write_before_and_after.cob pins LINAGE-COUNTER 001 -> 004 for `BEFORE AFTER ADVANCING 3 LINES`. || code sites: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/IO/SequentialConnector.cs#PositionOnLogicalPage (`LinageCounter += lines`), #Write (the plain arm's GR7c3 single line), #WriteAdvancing (the one print-control arm, which counts the phrase's single amount).

[folded GR-13.18.34.4-L2.3 = §13.18.34.4 7) c) 3.: CONFORMS]
BOTH ARMS OF THE DISPATCH INCREMENT BY ONE. A LINAGE file is line-oriented from its first write, so the record-sequential shape reroutes at :339 into WriteAdvancing with lines = 1 and the line-sequential/varying shape calls AdvanceLinageCounter(1) directly at :354 - the two-arm-dispatch question was asked and both arms answer. The named test pins the record-sequential arm (LINAGE-COUNTER 2 after one plain WRITE); the line-sequential arm was probed at <lane3 scratch>/out-b3/probe/linage/p23_sum.cob, where three plain WRITEs on a 2-line body wrap the page exactly once. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/IO/SequentialConnector.cs:339 (a LINAGE file's plain WRITE reroutes to WriteAdvancing(..., 1, before: true)) and :354 (AdvanceLinageCounter(1) on the line-sequential/varying path)

[folded GR-13.18.34.4-L2.4 = §13.18.34.4 7) c) 4.: CONFORMS]
BOTH SENTENCES MEASURED. 7c4 (reset to one at each succeeding logical page) is the named test - an advance of 4 from line 4 of a 5-line body lands on 1, not on the modulo carry 3. 7d (set to one at OPEN OUTPUT) is conformance-test:WiseOwl.Cobol.Tests.Conformance.LinageConformanceTests.Gr7d_CounterIsOneAtOpenOutput, and the OPEN arm is guarded on FileOpenMode.Output so INPUT / EXTEND / I-O do not reset it (14.9.27.3 SR2 forbids EXTEND on a LINAGE file outright). COST DISCLOSURE: what is verified is the COUNTER value; the physical repositioning that 7c4 names as its trigger - 'to the first line that may be written on' the next page - is defective whenever a margin is specified, and that is recorded against GR4/GR5, not here. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/IO/SequentialConnector.cs:168-175 (overflow: LinageCounter = 1, never a modulo carry) and :269-273 (OPEN OUTPUT: EvaluateLinage then LinageCounter = 1, EndOfPage = false)
